source.label: Zak Dolan's Worlds Diary (Wizards, Magic Arcana, 26 Aug 2004)

notes.text: Played at Gen Con '94 (MECCA Convention Center) under the rules that later became Type 1; the event was not called Type 1 at the time. Single elimination throughout: qualifying heats of 64 over two days, the 64 heat winners playing down to a champion on Sunday.

Date: the finals (round of 64 to the final) were played on the Sunday of Gen Con, per Rosewater's Gen Con report (The Duelist #3, reprinted by Wizards in 2004). Rosewater dates the convention only to 'late August' (arriving on the Thursday); MTG Wiki gives the championship as 19-21 August 1994, whose Sunday is 21 August. The exact day rests on that.

Players: 512 (the 512 slots, per Rosewater and the Duelist Companion recap). MTG Wiki gives 516. Dolan's diary describes four qualifiers of 128 with 16 advancing from each; the Companion recap describes eight heats of 64 with one winner each. Both total 512.

Only the semifinalists are known. The quarterfinal losers are not named in any source found (Dolan's diary says only that a fourth European player was knocked out by a countryman earlier); so this file has four players, not eight. No third-place match was reported; MTG Wiki's 3rd (Symens) and 4th (de Foucaud) are not from a primary source, so both are 3-4.
Semifinals: Dolan def. Symens 2-0, Lestrée def. DeFoucand 2-1; final Dolan def. Lestrée 2-1 (Duelist Companion recap and The Duelist #3).
No archetype names: the sources print none. The Dojo later called Dolan's deck 'Dolanesque' and Lestrée's 'Proto-Zoo'.

Lists for Symens and DeFoucand exist only on mtgtop8 (event 9186, filed as Standard, dated 01/08/94) and MTG Wiki, which cites mtgtop8; neither names an original source, and de Foucaud's mtgtop8 main deck is 66 cards. They are not copied here.
From USA (Rolla, Missouri). The diary's list is the deck after he changed it between the qualifier and the finals (he says he cut Balance and Steal Artifact and added Chaos Orb to the sideboard).

61 cards. The diary prints 60 (headed '60 cards') without Sylvan Library, but the same diary says 'Bertrand was playing 61 cards' (so he could still have 60 after tearing up Chaos Orb), the card-by-card recap of the final shows him casting Sylvan Library in game 1 before any sideboarding, and his Duelist profile names 'the Sylvan Library'. Sylvan Library is added from those; MTG Wiki also lists 61 with it.
Spelled 'Lestree' in the diary and The Duelist #3 and 'Lestreé' in the 2004 Wizards feature. French National Champion, from Pantin, France.
From Brussels, Belgium. Lost the semifinal to Dolan 2-0. Dolan's diary says his sideboard included Gloom, Gloom, Flashfires, Flashfires and three Tsunami; no full list from a primary source.

Spelled 'DeFoucand' in The Duelist #3 and every Wizards page; mtgtop8 and MTG Wiki spell him 'Cyrille de Foucaud'. The primary spelling is kept; which is right was not verified. From Paris, France. Lost the semifinal to Lestrée 2-1.

notes.text: Held at AndCon '95, Seagate Convention Center, Toledo. The Duelist gives the championship as Sept. 29-Oct. 1; the Andon press release gives the convention as Sept. 28-Oct. 1. The day of the Top 8 and final is not stated anywhere found: the date here is the last day of the convention and is not verified.

Its standing was disputed beforehand: on rec.games.trading-cards.magic.misc (Aug 1995) a player complains that the AndCon flyer listed a Type I National, that a Wizards customer-service rep then said there was not one, and that Andon's press release promised 'national championships'. The Duelist reported it as the Type I National Championship.

The Duelist mentions 'the top eight' decks (three had no basic lands) but names only the two finalists and prints no lists. No other Top 8 names, no lists, and no attendance were found. The Dojo's 'Chip Hogan Barrier deck' is his Origins '95 list, which the Dojo calls only 'quite similar' to his AndCon deck; it is not used.

From Dallas, TX. Beat Bentley 3-0 in the final. The Duelist describes the deck (all colors but black, no basic lands, Counterspells, Icy Manipulators, Relic Barriers, Winter Orbs, Erhnam Djinns, Mishra's Factories, Fireballs, Glasses of Urza, Chaos Orb, Hydroblasts) but prints no list. 'Aikido deck' is Hogan's own description.
From Rochester, NY. The Duelist describes a red/white deck with Armageddon, Balance, Blood Moon, Land Tax, Jalum Tome, Serra Angels and Juggernauts; no list.

notes.text: Lists and player names copied from mtgtop8, which took them from the organizer's (Card Titan's) Melee page; the lists were not compared card for card against Melee.

Placings and seeds are from the organizer's Melee page: seeds are the standings after the last Swiss round, and placings follow its playoff matches (quarterfinals: Max Gilmore def. mbatista 2-0; Chad Uzzell def. Stefan Vastek 2-1; Dave Kaplan def. andrewslafreniere 2-0; Jeremy Henry def. Greg Mitchell 2-0. Semifinals: Dave Kaplan def. Chad Uzzell 2-0; Jeremy Henry def. Max Gilmore 2-0. Final: Jeremy Henry def. Dave Kaplan 2-0). They agree with mtgtop8's at every tier.
Swiss was played on 2025-10-10; mtgtop8 dates the event to that day. The Top 8 was played on 2025-10-11.
Archetype names are MTGGoldfish's, for consistency across events.

notes.text: The organizer (4Seasons Tournaments) posted the Top 8 lists only as photos on X, which could not be opened; the event ran in the Companion app, so there is no Melee or MTGGoldfish tournament page. The lists are mtgtop8's transcription.

Placings are from the organizer's two VODs of the Top 8: quarterfinals Chen def. Bastianelli, Javier David def. Cioffini, Sørlie def. Ratkowski, Cicchini def. Ronkainen (recap at about 11:21:50 in part 1); semifinal Chen def. Javier David (part 1); final Cicchini def. Chen 2-0 (part 2). The other semifinal, Cicchini def. Sørlie, was not streamed and follows from the bracket. They agree with mtgtop8's. Seeds are the order of the organizer's "TOP 8" post, which is the Swiss standing, not the result.
Part 2 of the VOD: the final.
The organizer's Top 8 post, in seed order.

The organizer's schedule had the Vintage Championship on Friday 28 November from 10:00; the Top 8 lists were posted at 06:41 UTC on 29 November, so the Top 8 may have finished that morning. Players: 236 per the organizer's tweet as cited by mtgtop8; MTGGoldfish says about 233.
MTGGoldfish spells him "Jorgen Sorli", and mtgtop8 has him as "Jørgen Sørli" at other events.

notes.text: melee.gg refuses automated requests, so the lists were copied from mtgtop8, which took them from Melee (event 77979). MTGGoldfish's copy agrees card for card, and the four decks Hareruya also published match too.

The cut was to a Top 16. These are the eight quarterfinalists of the playoff. Hareruya's "トップ8デッキリスト" is a different set, the top eight after the Swiss (Okamoto, Del Pivo, Perrini, Yamaguchi, Morita, Sekimoto, Miura, Yueh), and is not used. Seeds are Swiss ranks from Hareruya's Top 16 profiles, which also give the names in Japanese.

Organized by Hareruya, who confirm Okamoto as champion; the 2nd, 3-4 and 5-8 placings are mtgtop8's and MTGGoldfish's playoff order. mtgtop8 and MTGGoldfish date the event 13 December, the UTC date of its 08:30 JST start on the 14th.
Archetype names are MTGGoldfish's, for consistency across events.
